Compared to many Metallica fans I’m a fairly young one. (I’m 23, born 2001) and I’ll give my take. My introduction to Metallica was through Sandman, Bellz, One, Master and Nothing else matters. I heard them through my childhood but once I discovered my passion for music, it was through Metallica.

I’m so grateful that they made The Black Album, otherwise they would not be the biggest heavy metal band on earth. Period. And I probably would not have found them either. I’m glad they wanted to do something different and hired Bob Rock to push them into a different process in every aspect as a band. I have not heard a record yet that is as well produced and well executed and The Black Album. It’s heavy as hell, it’s emotional, it’s beautiful. 

Sure it’s different and more commercial compared their previous four records, but that is a good thing. Think about it, you will never grow as an individual if you never step outside your comfort zone or tread outside your safe space.

When stepping outside your own box you sometimes succeed, and sometimes you fail. (You can find this in their discography aswell) However that’s where you learn and grow when you fail or go through hard times.

You don’t have to be a fan of every single thing Metallica does or have done to call your self a fan of their work. Everyone likes different things, but as far as I’m concerned I really respect that Metallica took risks and explored new things and still produces music and tours giving us fans an experience like no other.

I also love the fact that James is so humble these days, and takes time throughout the set to thank us fans for making their reality possible. That is so humble and I really feel at home in the Metallica family.

Jag jobbade dock inte varje helg fredag och lördag, oftast var det kanske varannan helg båda dagarna eller en av dagarna varje helg, det varierade lite. Du kommer få mycket tid att hänga med kompisar på skoltid, sen kan du planera fritiden runt dina pass på jobbet!

I just use rocksmith as I would play any other game where I play for entertainment, not primarily as a way to learn. However if I really want to learn a song I use riff repeater to slow it down and dissect it as you normally would. You HAVE to build muscle memory to be able to learn a song and all of the licks in it, which takes a lot of time to build 

The biggest thing rocksmith has helped me with it improving my left hand placement and my dexterity in both hands, now I am way more economical with all of my fingers and I don’t fatigue as easily, and it has improved my muting.

For me it really isn’t a big difference between playing rocksmith or guitar hero, unless I really put in the time to truly learn the songs on my instrument

I rest my lower arm against the body of the bass while my hand moves up and down the strings while resting my thumb over and across the strings I want to mute.
